premises.text: Development environments never match production, so engineers waste time chasing bugs they should not have to fix
premises.evidence_span: our development environments never matched up with our production environments

premises.text: Long-running tests leave engineers idle and unproductive while they wait
premises.evidence_span: when your tests take a long time to run, your engineers essentially are not doing work

premises.text: Build breaks block the entire team from doing work
premises.evidence_span: When a build break happens, your entire team is blocked from doing work

premises.text: Quality holds each pushed change in limbo isolation, spins up production-like cloud replicas, and runs the automation suite in parallel so changes are tested like production without breaking the shared build
premises.evidence_span: it takes that change and holds it in a limbo state. So this first isolates it from all the other engineers on his team

premises.text: Making existing engineers more effective is a better path to capacity than external hiring because finding talent is hard
premises.evidence_span: Instead of looking externally at the problem, perhaps we should turn to the engineers we already have and look internally

domains.name: Quality isolation and parallel testing platform

value.text: Unleash engineers and make development teams substantially more effective
value.evidence_span: quality can make your development team 20% more effective

secondary_value.text: Happier engineers who like their jobs more when they are more effective
secondary_value.evidence_span: if you make us happier, or if you make us more effective, you make us much, much happier

causal_links.evidence_span: this clearly isn't good for productivity
this gives the test really fast turnaround time, and it means devs don't have to wait for tests
quality can make your development team 20% more effective
